[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Number of Different Subsequences GCDs** [LC 1819 · Number of Different Subsequences GCDs](https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-different-subsequences-gcds/){difficulty="Hard"}

Enumerating $2^n$ subsequences is hopeless, but the *set of gcd values* is tiny: folding a
gcd over a growing set can only produce divisors of numbers already in the array. That
gives two views. The **forward** view folds a set - keep the set of gcds of subsequences
seen so far, and when a new element $x$ arrives the only new gcds are $x$ itself and
$\gcd(g, x)$ for each existing $g$; the set stays small because gcds collapse fast. The
**backward** view asks a different question: for a target $d$, is $d$ achievable? Exactly
when the gcd of *all array elements that are multiples of $d$* equals $d$ - because their
subsequence gcd is the finest thing a multiple-of-$d$ subsequence can reach. Sieving the
value domain by divisibility (@sec-gcd-a4) turns that into a $\sum_d V/d$ harmonic loop.

[Solved in full in @sec-gcd-p3-subseq.]{.card-link}

:::
